lawyer:
Mian Abdul Gafur---------For the appellant.

Afser Molla and another-------- Appellants.
Abdul Aziz & others---------- Respondents.
full_judgment: 5. Mr. Miah Abdul Gaffar the learned Advocate for the defendant appellants argues that the judgment passed by the District Judge in the appeal is not a proper judgment of reversal. He further argued that the lower appellate court ought to have found that Hakirojan and Akubjan had never any possession in the suit land and that in 1939 A. D. defendant No. 4 Afsar Ali Molla got possession of the suit land after taking delivery of possession as per writ of delivery of possession Ext. C through Court in Certificate Case No. 1541/35-36. He further argued that as defendant No. 4 was not in possession of the suit; properties before 1344 B. S. (corresponding to 1939 A.D.), he was not liable merely because of kot. kabala Ext. 2 dated 7.10.33; to pay rents for the suit land under the provisions of section 76(c) of the Transfer of Property Act. He further argued that the lower appellate court ought not to have relied upon the deposition Ext. 6 given by defendant No. 4 Afsar Ali Molla in Title Suit No, 240 of 1953. He further argued that the lower appellate court ought to have held that as Akubjan and Hakim-jail had no physical possession in the suit land, they had no right to give mortgage to defendant No. 4 Afsar Ali Molla, his son defendant No. 5 Azintuddin, defendant No. l's father Mobarak and defendant No. 4's wife Robjan. He further argued that as there were four mortgagees under kot kabala Ext. 2, defendant No. 4 alone had no liability to pay the entire rent for the suit land or for the suit khatian. He further argued that by virtue of auction purchase in Certificate Case No. 1541/35-36 for arrears of rent as per sale certificate D appellant defendant No. 4 Afsar Ali Molla got an irredeemable title in the suit land and that with the said auction sale the equity of redemption was extinguished. He further argued that even if for the sake of argument it is admitted that the mortgage executed by Akubjan and Hakimjan in favour of defendant No. 4 Afsar Ali Molla and three others became a usufructury mortgage due to the amendment in the B.T. Act in 1938 by insertion of sub-section 1(a) in section 26 G of the B. T. Act, the mortgagors Akubjan and Hakimjan or their heirs ought to have taken possession of the suit land within 12 years after the expiry of the period of 15 years in 1948 and that by virtue of adverse possession for more than 12 years since 1948 the title of defendant No. 4 Afsar Ali Mona in the suit land has been perfected and that the claim for redemption of mortgage under the mortgage deed Ext. 2 is barred by limitation. He further argued that the lower appellate court ought. to have held that the transfer of their interest in the suit land by plaintiffs 1-3 to plaintiff 4 by registered kabala Ext. 1 is a collusive and sham transaction without consideration and that the lower appellate court ought to have taken into consideration the effect of the evidence of the witness for the defendant and the exhibits filed by them.
